source: Root-operated board results downloaded by root, independently parsed and cross-checked by backup_audit. Runtime library identity and capture IRQ delta remain operator reports, not proven by these four raw files.

operator_reported_capture_replay.captured_wrapper_version: v4; the private capture filename contains v5 and is not the runtime version authority
operator_reported_capture_replay.inference: The private captured stream decoded successfully with fresh WC v5/backend v4. This does not uniquely identify the cause of earlier failures.
operator_reported_capture_replay.ve_irq_delta_scope: Operator report only; raw replay JSON has no IRQ fields

operator_reported_first_webpage_measurem.cpu_percent_unit: 100 percent equals one fully used CPU core

software_regression_reference.kind: Actual candidate ARM64 libraries under QEMU with a stub client; no hardware access

interpretation_limits: Raw result files are bound and internally checked. Runtime lib maps/hashes, capture IRQ64 and heap state are still operator reports unless separately bound.
The current source is approximately 30 fps. These observations do not establish 60 fps playback.
The first rVFC measurement counts main-thread callback deliveries, not physical display presentation.
The corrected rVFC metadata presentedFrames counter describes browser/compositor submission; it still does not prove physical display scanout.
totalVideoFrames minus droppedVideoFrames is a browser counter difference, not a display presentation measurement.
IRQ, CPU and video sampling windows are not perfectly synchronized; IRQ and frame increments must not be interpreted as exact one-to-one correspondence.
Short bounded observations do not establish long-term MSE, repeated seek, codec/configuration change, memory-budget or production stability.
The 128 MiB private heap quarantine and lack of proven DMA drain or IOMMU isolation remain unchanged.
Historical approximately 120 MiB usage is not a fresh-boot current-usage measurement.
No raw user media, authentication data or private vendor libraries are embedded in this record.
Process CPU selection matches all Firefox processes by command line, not solely a verified candidate process tree.
First raw measurement retains the legacy effective_delivered_fps field. Its name is misleading; it is not used as physical presentation evidence.
Corrected rVFC metadata reports about31.07fps for an approximately30fps source; browser API counters and callback timing do not by themselves measure unique displayed source frames.

corrected_webpage_measurement.cpu_percent_unit: 100 percent equals one fully used CPU core
corrected_webpage_measurement.all_sampled_video_states: 1920x1080, rate1, playing, no video error; monotonic sampled media time and total frame counter
corrected_webpage_measurement.presented_frames_note: rVFC metadata increased958 while totalVideoFrames increased926 over nearby windows. 31.0702fps is retained as an API observation, not accepted physical presentation or unique source-frame rate.

independent_checks: All64 hardware frame MD5 values exactly equal software reference in order.
Hardware output PTS list exactly equals sorted original input packet PTS; raw elementary-stream framemd5 PTS are synthetic and were not used as actual timestamps.
Replay records SHA-256 matches the retained private input records.
Both webpage IRQ/counter/media deltas recomputed from raw endpoints.
Second sample denominator and browser non-dropped/rVFC metadata rates recomputed from their recorded windows.
No paused/error/dimension/rate change or backwards media time/counter observed in sampled snapshots; the instrumentation lacks a permanent video-element identity token.
